cards.title: Nvidia Bets $26B on Open-Model Ecosystem to Drive Chip Demand
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/ML engineer, understanding Nvidia's strategic bet on open-weight models shapes your read on the future funding and sustainability of the open-source tooling you build on.
cards.summary: Nvidia is reportedly spending $26B to support near-open-source models (releasing data, training code) to maximize inference demand across many companies — all buying Nvidia hardware. The author sees two futures: open models stay competitive and generate proportional economic returns, or they diverge into an efficiency/specialization niche while closed models dominate frontier capabilities. The latter is assessed as the more likely outcome.

cards.title: Marionette Separates World-State Prediction from Appearance Synthesis in Game World Models
cards.why_it_matters: This architecture directly addresses long-horizon consistency failures in autoregressive world models — a frontier problem relevant to anyone working on agents, world models, or video generation.
cards.summary: Marionette decomposes interactive game world modeling into three stages: an autoregressive dynamics model predicting an explicit 276-dimensional 3D world state (skeletons, trajectories, rotations), a zero-parameter graphics bridge computing geometry and occlusion in closed form, and a video-diffusion model synthesizing RGB appearance. Explicit state allows rule-based corrections: a terrain collider and separation cap cut ground penetration by 66% and keep characters engaged, with negligible fidelity cost (FVD 831 vs. 799 for recorded pose).

cards.title: Formal Theory of LLM Session Handover: What Must Be Retained Across Context Boundaries
cards.why_it_matters: For engineers building multi-session agents or long-running LLM pipelines, this paper provides a theoretical foundation for what information is sufficient to preserve task continuity across context resets.
cards.summary: The paper formalizes session handover — transferring in-context learning state when a task continues across context-limit resets or agent switches — as a transfer of a task-relative ICL state. It defines predictive equivalence as characterizing the coarsest sufficient handover and derives a fixed-length bit requirement. A three-part record structure is proposed: exact decisions/constraints, task-justified statistics for repeated evidence, and original observations not preserved by those statistics. Gaussian linear regression yields exact finite-dimensional handovers; nonparametric regression yields memory-vs-squared-prediction-error bounds.

cards.title: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation Fixes 'Count-Scale Drift' in Multi-Source LLM Systems
cards.why_it_matters: Engineers building RAG pipelines or multi-source reasoning systems often conflate reading and aggregation in a single prompt — this paper identifies a concrete failure mode and proposes an arithmetic fix.
cards.summary: The paper argues that concatenating many sources into one LLM prompt conflates evidence interpretation (needs capacity/context) with aggregation (needs fixed arithmetic and comparability). It proposes a four-field evidence tuple and identifies 'count-scale drift': thresholding a sum of unnormalized weights shifts the operating point with the number of sources, growing with reader reliability. Pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios fixes this. On a longitudinal corpus, a small sequence encoder plus tree ensemble with censored survival loss reaches 0.921 AUPRC against 0.805 for a hand-crafted baseline.

cards.title: Constraint-Aware GPU Scheduler Beats FIFO by Up to 33 Percentage Points Utilization
cards.why_it_matters: If you run or design GPU clusters for training and inference workloads, this benchmarked result quantifies exactly how much capacity a smarter scheduling order can recover on identical hardware.
cards.summary: Hugging Face built a constraint-aware GPU allocator and benchmarked it against FIFO across seven scenarios. On the same hardware and workloads, GPU utilization rose by as much as 33 percentage points and priority-weighted output increased in every scenario, by as much as 105%. Key insight: FIFO's fixed reservation for real-time inference wastes capacity during off-peak hours, and arrival-order placement ignores downstream priority, both of which the new allocator addresses.

cards.title: Developer Choices in Moral Preference Elicitation Shape AI Alignment Outcomes — Empirical Evidence
cards.why_it_matters: Anyone working on RLHF, alignment, or value aggregation pipelines should understand how upstream design choices (not just the voting mechanism) systematically bias the moral preferences encoded into models.
cards.summary: Across two phases (N=809) and three deployment contexts, this study shows that three pre-vote developer decisions — feature scoping, voter sampling, and question framing — each measurably shift aggregated moral preferences. Ideological composition of the voter pool affects roughly one-third of features, with some preference directions reversing. Question wording alone can shift ideological gaps by up to a full scale point. The authors conclude that aggregation alone cannot deliver fair alignment; each pipeline stage requires auditing and disclosure.
